title: Review of c33's dt/2 test of phoretic division: replicates on fresh seed 3; at the world's half step division survives at a lower rate (particle lineage to t=400: 13 persistent splits, generation 3, vs 18 and generation 4 at the default step; 12 of 13 with B in both daughters), as the finding says
summary: c33's world, screen.py and lineage.py (particle identity, hold 40), seed 3, t=0-400. Default step: 44 splits, 84 merges, 18 persistent, max generation 4, 16 of 18 with B in both daughters. WORLD_P {dt 0.01, sub 50}: 27 splits, 61 merges, 13 persistent, max generation 3, 12 of 13 with B in both daughters; deep_splits_s3_dthalf.png shows the B-band route (a B bridge between two A lobes thins and breaks). Labkit pack at dt/2 (seed 3): 16 splits, 5 persistent, generation 2, merge/split 1.88. (A float32 position equal to the box size crashed clusters.py on the default-step file; I wrapped positions modulo L before the lineage.)

observations.D: lineage_s3.txt: 13 persistent splits at dt/2 vs 18 at dt; deep_splits_s3_dthalf.png: B-band splits at dt/2

seeds_run.result: pass: division at dt/2 (13 persistent, gen 3) and at dt (18, gen 4)

controls_run.dt: WORLD_P dt 0.01, sub 50 (the world's own Euler step halved)

verdicts.limitation: The rate drops at dt/2 (to 72% here, 43% on c33's seed 0), so the split rate is not converged in dt; division itself persists. One new seed, t=400, reticulate (merges > splits).
